newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines denies visa to Timorese Nobel laureate.
newsitem.headline: Philippines denies visa to Timorese Nobel laureate.

text.p: The Philippines has again blocked East Timorese Nobel laureate Jose Ramos-Horta from entering the country, the presidential palace said.
The palace said in a statement received on Wednesday that the decision was taken by a cabinet committee "on the basis of national interest".
The Manila Times newspaper said the step was taken to avoid embarrassing Indonesia, a close ally of the Philippines.
Ramos-Horta, an outspoken campaigner for freedom for the Indonesia-ruled territory of East Timor, was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize along with East Timorese Bishop Carlos Belo.

The Philippines previously barred Ramos-Horta, who lives in self-exile in Australia, from entering the country in November last year at the time of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit.
Both the Philippines and Indonesia are members of APEC.
The palace said Ramos-Horta had applied for a visa to attend a human rights seminar which began in Manila on Tuesday and is to last until January 28.
It said the government "invoked a constitutional provision as well as other existing laws which allow it to deny entry to foreigners to protect its national interests".

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later. The United Nations does not recognise Jakarta as the ruler of the territory and still considers Portugal as the administering power.
